text:
Maya: sketching a unified warmup/orchestration approach for different weight sources. goal: deterministic activation semantics + minimal per-format surface. dumping thoughts here.

Liam: short Q: do we want the worker to own warmup decisions or a separate warmup coordinator service?

Maya: worker-owned state machine preferred for locality (fast decisions, fewer RPCs). coordinator only hands credits/priorities and listens for health events.

Devin: ok. what's the shape of the state machine?

Maya: current proposal: 
```
States: IDLE -> RESOLVE -> HEADER_SCAN -> INDEX_TRY -> CHUNK_PREFETCH -> KVCACHE_APPLY -> CONSISTENCY_CHECK -> ACTIVE
Errors -> RETRY/FAIL
```
Transitions annotated by adapter flags: supports_index_first, zero_copy_ok, prefix_safe.

Sara: for prefix_safe activation we should define an "activation window" concept — max_allowed_unverified_tokens per model route so users don't get long hallucinating responses while verify runs.

Liam: activation window sounds useful. default small for hosted, zero for strict enterprise. Also need backpressure: if prefetch_budget exhausted we should deprioritize low-priority models.

Maya: agree. adding fields: priority_score, soft_deadline_ms. state machine will signal "soft_activate" vs "hard_activate". soft_activate allows gated ops only.

Devin: adapters: keep tiny. propose callback set: probe(meta)->capabilities, open(range)->stream, verify_stream(async)->verify_result, finalize(). adapters return lightweight per-file manifests when present.

Sara: how do we handle mixed-file bundles where some files can prefix-activate and others cannot?

Maya: treat bundle as composed of subunits. state machine runs per-subunit and aggregates readiness. ACTIVE only when critical subunits are verified or marked non-critical. add manifest flag `critical=true/false` per file.

Liam: telemetry requests: emit tags for activation_type (soft/hard), verify_duration_ms, prefetch_bytes, retries, eviction_cancels. also expose a sample of partial-kv entries written for inspect.

Devin: eviction: if eviction triggers while in KVCACHE_APPLY or VERIFY, we should cancel and either resume later or roll back. propose: warmup run carries a monotonic warmup_id and checkpoint snapshot token; on eviction we persist a minimal resume token (last applied chunk index) so retries can resume without starting over.

Sara: resume token is good. also add a TTL: if resume delayed > resume_ttl then we restart full path to ensure consistency.

Maya: security edgecases: encrypted shards. adapter surface needs `requires_decrypt` and `kms_key_ref`. verify_stream should accept decrypted bytes only. for KMS we allow prefetch to request a decrypt lease from key-mgmt layer.

Liam: what about partial checksums? can we trust a prefix-based checksum to verify some layers?

Maya: adopt layered checksums: per-chunk checksum + per-layer summary hash. progressive verify will validate chunk checksums as they arrive; full consistency check validates layer summary. state machine will annotate which layers are verified.

Devin: kvcache integration: kvcache.accept_prefix(layer, offset, blob, resume_token). kvcache must mark entries with `verified=false` initially if only prefix applied. runtime will consult kvcache.is_verified(layer) before using long-context attention.

Sara: tests: 1) safetensors with index file present (fast path) 2) safetensors streaming with chunk checksums 3) local mmap zero-copy 4) mixed-critical bundle 5) eviction+resume token expiry 6) encrypted shard handshake. I'll draft infra test harness.

infra-bot: canary deploy: branch warmup-unified-2026-03 pushed to staging.

Liam: UX: expose model-state in console: inactive / soft-active / hard-active plus percent-verified and resume_token age. ops want to see failed retries and last_eviction_ts.

Maya: agree console fields and alerts. also Integrate Optimize to surface models with frequent soft-activations (suggest indexing or smaller shard sizes).

Devin: one more performance angle: if many concurrent requests target prefix-activated models we need an admission controller to cap sequence length and throttle token emission until verification closes.

Sara: yes. add admission_limit per warmup run and a gate that enforces max_tokens_outstanding.

Maya: I'll write RFC with diagrams + adapter interface + state enum + metrics list. planning to mark behaviour: hosted default=soft-active, dedicated default=hard-active. posting draft later today.

Liam: thanks. I'll add notes about manifest-synthesis for legacy bundles (on-demand TOC by probing ranges).

Devin: fine. edgecase: transport flaps (partial reads). adapters should expose retryable vs fatal errors so state machine can pick backoff.

Sara: noted. I'll include test vectors and a small harness for simulated network stalls.

Maya: great. ping me any other edgecases. :sparkles:
